articles.title: Reunions with teacher and former helper stir emotions online
articles.summary: A teacher’s kindness helped shape Dino Isaac’s life, while a former helper who raised Leticia Peh ended up sacrificing more than the girl imagined. Their reunions, featured in On The Red Dot, have struck a chord with viewers. Reunions with teacher and former helper stir emotions online.

articles.title: Cheap to burn, costly to bear: What fuels Indonesia’s persistent cycle of fires and haze?
articles.summary: Wildfires in Indonesia have caused transboundary haze and disrupted livelihoods in Sumatra. In the last of a three-part series, CNA looks at why the fires persist despite bans and crackdowns - and what it will take to stamp them out for good. Cheap to burn, costly to bear: What fuels Indonesia’s persistent cycle of fires and haze?

articles.title: Zelenskyy, at UN, urges leaders to keep choking Russia’s revenues and impede its war efforts
articles.summary: ‘When someone gives Russia more money through trade, they give this war more time; and that is exactly why we insist on limiting trade with the aggressor, and why we are burning Russia's revenues ourselves,’ said Volodymyr Zelenskyy Zelenskyy, at UN, urges leaders to keep choking Russia’s revenues and impede its war efforts.

articles.title: Trump's Board of Peace proposes $2.45 billion blueprint to begin Gaza reconstruction
articles.summary: At a meeting of the group’s board in New York on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly, the governors unveiled a 66-project blueprint to get things started while acknowledging enormous hurdles that must still be overcome Trump's Board of Peace proposes $2.45 billion blueprint to begin Gaza reconstruction.

articles.title: Iranian advisers helped Houthis seize Yemen's Red Sea coast in less than 48 hours: report
articles.summary: The key port city of Mokha was abandoned as residents left in the night, allowing the Houthis to roll in unopposed on September 10. Their seizure of strategic islands nearby further enhanced their ability to attack Saudi oil shipments in the Red Sea Iranian advisers helped Houthis seize Yemen's Red Sea coast in less than 48 hours: report.

articles.title: Soorya Krishnamoorthy, who dedicated his life to promote arts, passes away in Keralam
articles.summary: The Soorya Stage and Film Society founded by him has been bringing the best of musicians, dancers and films to Thiruvananthapuram in Keralam every year without fail as part of the Soorya Music, Dance and Film Festival Soorya Krishnamoorthy, who dedicated his life to promote arts, passes away in Keralam.

articles.title: Five Afghan Family Members Die Of Thirst While Trying To Reach Iran
articles.summary: An Afghan migrant reported that his stepmother and four sisters died An Afghan migrant has told RFE/RL's Radio Azadi that his stepmother and four sisters died of thirst and hunger while attempting a dangerous journey to Iran after economic hardship forced the family to leave Afghanistan again. Five Afghan Family Members Die Of Thirst While Trying To Reach Iran.

articles.title: Delcy Rodríguez poses with Trump in New York as Maduro languishes in jail nearby
articles.summary: Venezuela’s interim president hails ‘historic meeting’ and does not say whether she will visit snatched predecessorVenezuela’s interim president, Delcy Rodríguez, has celebrated a “historic” meeting with Donald Trump in New York, posing for a smiley photo with the US president, less than nine months after he ordered the abduction of her boss, Nicolás Maduro. Delcy Rodríguez poses with Trump in New York as Maduro languishes in jail nearby.

articles.title: Zelenskyy urges stronger pressure on Russia, warns war’s impact is spreading beyond Ukraine
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Wednesday called for intensified pressure on Russia to end its war against Ukraine, arguing that Moscow continues to incur massive losses while prolonging a conflict whose consequences are increasingly being felt far beyond the battlefield. Zelenskyy urges stronger pressure on Russia, warns war’s impact is spreading beyond Ukraine.

articles.title: OpenAI and Anthropic brief Security Council amid ‘real and imminent’ threat posed by runaway AI
articles.summary: The Security Council has been briefed by some of the world's top AI executives on the huge benefits and huge risks the frontier technology presents. With warnings mounting that the world may be losing its grip on systems built to outthink us, Yoshua Bengi, a recipient of the prestigious Turing Award and one of the Godfathers of machine intelligence, said the dangers of AI beyond human control repr.

articles.title: Climate change is here - What happens next is still in our hands
articles.summary: 🔴 LIVE NOW From deadly floods in the Himalayas to wildfires and extreme heat across Europe, 2026 has brought a succession of stark reminders of a changing climate. The task is immediate: Protect people from the impacts already unfolding while rapidly cutting the emissions of harmful gasses driving climate change. World leaders are meeting today to discuss how to turn those priorities into action.

articles.title: UN’s ‘sacred covenant has been broken’, Argentina’s Milei tells General Assembly
articles.summary: Argentine President Javier Milei told the General Assembly on Wednesday that the UN has broken the “sacred covenant” on which it was founded, failing at what it was meant to do – while excelling at things beyond its remit. UN’s ‘sacred covenant has been broken’, Argentina’s Milei tells General Assembly.

articles.title: World leaders debate ongoing war in Ukraine
articles.summary: Five years of war. Another winter closing in. Today, the Security Council once again debates a path to peace – though any resolution still runs up against the veto of Russia, one of its own permanent members, whose objections have repeatedly stalled any consensus. As world leaders take the floor, the gap between diplomatic process and battlefield reality appears to be stark.

articles.title: DR Congo Ebola outbreak toll exceeds 3,700 deaths
articles.summary: More than 130 days into the latest Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), health experts said on Wednesday that response efforts have been scaled up significantly and “the first encouraging signs of progress” are now being seen. DR Congo Ebola outbreak toll exceeds 3,700 deaths.

articles.title: US Set To Unveil Next Steps for Trump-Backed Armenia-Azerbaijan Transit Corridor
articles.summary: The United States is set to unveil the next stage of TRIPP, a planned transport corridor through southern Armenia that Washington says could open new trade routes linking the South Caucasus and Central Asia with Western markets. US Set To Unveil Next Steps for Trump-Backed Armenia-Azerbaijan Transit Corridor.

articles.title: ‘Super El Niño’ projected to cause 15,800 additional heat deaths in India, says report
articles.summary: The heaviest toll is expected in poorer countries, already struggling with food insecurity and high energy costs, partly due to climate change and the fallout of the war in Iran, the University of Chicago-based Climate Impact Lab says This year’s El Niño-driven heat could cause nearly half a million more deaths, group says. ‘This year’s El Niño is also a ‘postcard from our future’, bringing temperatures climate change is projected to deliver 20 years in the future.

Indian billionaire’s payments firm plots biggest London flotation in years.

articles.title: Iranian Hard-Liners Up In Arms After Araqchi-Witkoff Meeting In New York
articles.summary: Iranian hard‑liners condemned the meeting between US special envoy Steve Witkoff and Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi in New York on US special envoy Steve Witkoff and Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi met in New York on September 22 following days of signals that US-Iranian talks would take place on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly. The meeting sparked a backlash from Iranian hard-liners.

articles.title: Amid Setbacks In The Sahel, Russia Quietly Builds Ties In Madagascar
articles.summary: Russia’s efforts to cultivate clout in Africa’s Sahel have been a mixed bag of successes and setbacks. Across the continent, however, on the Indian Ocean island of Madagascar, Moscow is making another quiet push for influence. Amid Setbacks In The Sahel, Russia Quietly And Quickly Builds Ties In Madagascar. Amid Setbacks In The Sahel, Russia Quietly Builds Ties In Madagascar.

Trump, Zelenskyy Discuss Peace Negotiations, Potential Energy Cease-Fire.

articles.title: म्यांमार-यूएई से तस्करी कर सोना भारत लाने का आरोप, हवाला के जरिए खपाए जा रहे थे फर्जी बिल
articles.summary: प्रवर्तन निदेशालय (ED) के गुवाहाटी जोनल ऑफिस-I ने मनी लॉन्ड्रिंग के मामले में 37.064 किलोग्राम सोना और करीब 13 ग्राम चांदी जैसे धातु के फ्लेक्स को अस्थायी रूप से अटैच किया है. अटैच किए गए सोने की अनुमानित कीमत 54 करोड़ रुपये से अधिक बताई गई है. इसमें 29 बड़े आकार की सोने की छड़ें और 50 छोटे आकार के सोने के टुकड़े शामिल हैं.
